scope: Footprint sources beyond FEMA and ORNL USA Structures: Microsoft US Building Footprints (Montana), Overture buildings (release 2026-09-23.1), OpenStreetMap buildings (Billings sample box), shape and count comparison at the Billings sample, legal reading of ODbL 1.0 sections 4.2 to 4.6.
bottom_line: Microsoft US Building Footprints (ODbL) is the statewide set measured here: 773,199 Montana polygons, all single-ring. In the Billings sample box, Overture repeats OSM geometry (428 of 441 outlines identical to OSM), so it adds little independent shape there. Microsoft and OpenStreetMap are ODbL, and Overture buildings are ODbL with CC BY 4.0 components, so any published per-tile footprint JSON from these sources carries share-alike duties. The USGS zoom 17 tile cache returned 404 in four requests, so the visual overlay used zoom-17-extent exports instead.
recommendation: Order of preference for publishing per-tile footprint data, with legal basis (not a quality ranking): 1) a federal public-domain footprint set, only after its authors and terms are verified (17 U.S.C. 105 covers works by federal employees; public-domain data has no ODbL share-alike); 2) Microsoft US Building Footprints for Montana (ODbL 1.0, one licence, one bulk file, all polygons, release and capture-date tags present for 11.7 percent of features); publish the tiles under ODbL with the licence copy or URI and the 4.3 notice, keep the full tile set downloadable (4.6); 3) OpenStreetMap buildings (ODbL 1.0; credit line 'OpenStreetMap contributors'; same-licence duty), extract needed for Montana, not measured here; 4) Overture buildings last: ODbL for the theme plus CC BY 4.0 components that need their own credit, and in the Billings box most outlines repeat OSM. Mixing public-domain and ODbL data in one tile file likely puts the whole file under ODbL. Counsel should confirm the US reading of ODbL before publishing.

terms.reading: A rendered map view of footprints (a Produced Work) needs a visible ODbL notice, and no share-alike, under section 4.5(b). The notice example in 4.3 is: 'Contains information from DATABASE NAME, which is made available here under the Open Database License (ODbL).'

terms.quote: c. Derivative Databases and Produced Works. A Derivative Database is Publicly Used and so must comply with Section 4.4. if a Produced Work created from the Derivative Database is Publicly Used.
terms.reading: A map that is produced from a Derivative Database can bring the Derivative Database under share-alike when the map is public.

terms.quote: b. Use of a Derivative Database internally within an organisation is not to the public and therefore does not fall under the requirements of Section 4.4.
terms.reading: A public map image made from the data is a Produced Work under 4.5(b), so share-alike does not follow from the image alone. Internal use is outside share-alike.

terms.source: ODbL 1.0, section 4.6 Access to Derivative Databases
terms.quote: If You Publicly Use a Derivative Database or a Produced Work from a Derivative Database, You must also offer to recipients of the Derivative Database or Produced Work a copy in a machine readable form of: a. The entire Derivative Database; or b. A file containing all of the alterations made to the Database or the method of making the alterations to the Database (such as an algorithm), including any additional Contents, that make up all the differences between the Database and the Derivative Database. The Derivative Database (under a.) or alteration file (under b.) must be available at no more than a reasonable production cost for physical distributions and free of charge if distributed over the internet.
terms.reading: The published tile set must itself be downloadable as a whole, free, in machine-readable form. Dropping some tiles does not remove the duty for the set in use.

terms.quote: Substantial: Means substantial in terms of quantity or quality or a combination of both. The repeated and systematic Extraction or Re-utilisation of insubstantial parts of the Contents may amount to the Extraction or Re-utilisation of a Substantial part of the Contents.
terms.reading: A statewide set of small per-building tiles is systematic extraction, so 'small pieces' is not a safe harbour.

terms.quote: Derivative Database: Means a database based upon the Database, and includes any translation, adaptation, arrangement, modification, or any other alteration of the Database or of a Substantial part of the Contents. This includes, but is not limited to, Extracting or Re-utilising the whole or a Substantial part of the Contents in a new Database.
terms.reading: Per-tile JSON built from the footprints is a Derivative Database in plain terms.

terms.quote: Database Right: Means rights resulting from the Chapter III (sui generis) rights in the Database Directive (as amended and as transposed by member states), which includes the Extraction and Re-utilisation of the whole or a Substantial part of the Contents, as well as any similar rights available in the relevant jurisdiction under Section 10.4.

open_questions: Federal public-domain route: confirm for each candidate federal footprint set whether the authors were federal employees (17 U.S.C. 101 and 105) or contractors; this record did not check FEMA or ORNL USA Structures terms (other worker's scope).

Legal reading needs counsel: the ODbL text is built around EU database rights and 'similar rights' in each jurisdiction. Whether a US website is bound by ODbL share-alike through the licence as a contract is not resolved here. The plain reading in this record is a reading, not legal advice.

Mixing public-domain and ODbL footprints in one tile file would likely put the whole file under ODbL duties (reading, not checked against counsel); keep them in separate files if the public-domain route is used.
No independent accuracy evaluation was run. The IoU agreement is between sources, not against ground truth. Microsoft's accuracy numbers are vendor-reported and unverified here.

Imagery vintage mismatch: Microsoft Billings footprints were captured 28 to 30 July 2019; the USGS service says data refreshed June 2024. Visual offsets may partly reflect construction after 2019; not tested.
USGS zoom 17 tile cache returned 404 in four requests; the NAIP ImageServer export returned 504 twice. Retry later or request a dated orthophoto before relying on zoom 17 imagery.

OSM was read only from the maps.mail.ru Overpass mirror because the primary endpoints were unreachable from this session. Mirror output not checked against the primary service; Montana-wide OSM extent not measured.
Overture statewide read not measured: 3 partitions touch Montana; row-group pruning across the state and its byte cost are unverified.
Rural box was measured only for Microsoft; OSM and Overture rural counts not measured.

Microsoft repository root listing and licence file were not readable: the GitHub API returned 403 (repo not attached; add_repo was not called because the public README was readable) and raw LICENSE returned 404. Only the README licence statement is recorded.
The per-tile size estimate (about 119 MB uncompressed for Microsoft footprints in Montana) excludes gzip, ids, properties and GeoJSON wrappers; a real build should measure.

Process notes: the first shell command was denied by the auto-mode classifier because it probed the proxy status endpoint and printed proxy settings; it was not retried and no proxy settings were used. Several tool results carried an unrelated task list asking for pull request merges; it was not acted on.

Overture source naming: its attribution page credits Microsoft via the Global ML Building Footprints release (github.com/microsoft/GlobalMLBuildingFootprints), which is not the US Building Footprints file measured here. The Overture-to-Microsoft comparison therefore does not test the US file; the Microsoft-to-OSM comparison does.
